critique.summary: World v1 tests Witness B's claim at t=8.5s, while the car is still well up the approach. She testified she watched the car "right up until the moment it hit" (Depo 27:46). Re-timed to the moment she describes, the turning truck stands between her marked position and the car from about t=9.1s to impact. The world is patched and her claim must be re-tested.

findings.summary: The world checks Witness B's claim at the wrong moment: t=8.5s, 1.9 s before impact, instead of the final seconds she describes.
findings.detail: Her claim is not limited to the approach. At Depo 27:46 she says "I had a clear view of the car the whole way in. I watched it right up until the moment it hit. Nothing was in the way." and at Depo 28:17 "Yes. I saw it clearly, the whole time, right up until it went under the trailer. I'll never forget it.". The wit_B render at t=8.5s shows the car clearly, but at that moment the truck has not yet crossed in front of her. The observation time must cover the last seconds before impact (t≈9.9s; impact t=10.43s per the timeline built from HAR-17/02 p.29).

evidence.citation: wit_B.png @ t=8.5s (clear: truck not yet in the eastbound lanes)

findings.summary: From the position she marked on Exhibit 4, the truck-tractor and then the refrigerated van semitrailer block her view of the car from about t=9.1s until impact.
findings.detail: In the video at Depo 27:04 she says only "I was over by the corner, near the shelter." while marking an X at about (7.5, 6.5) m in the world frame, in front of the store near the bench shelter; at Depo 27:24 she says she was standing (eye 1.6 m). The truck turns left across both eastbound lanes (HAR-17/02 p.1, p.21), so its tractor and then its trailer pass between her and the westbound-facing view of the approaching car. The independent ray-cast agrees: clear at t=9s, blocked by veh_T_tractor then veh_T_trailer from t=9.1s. NTSB records the same effect for the real westbound witness: the semitrailer blocked his view of the car (HAR-17/02 p.1–2, p.29–30).

critique.summary: With Witness B at her Exhibit 4 mark and her claim tested at the moment she describes, the world matches the evidence. Her testimony that she watched the car "the whole way in" with "nothing in the way" is contradicted: the truck-tractor and then the refrigerated van semitrailer of Vehicle T block her line of sight for about the last 1.3 s before impact. No further patch is needed; the contradiction is in the testimony.

findings.summary: Witness B could not have watched the car up to impact from where she marked she was standing: Vehicle T's tractor, then its semitrailer, block her view from about t=9.1s.
findings.detail: Her eye-level render at t=9.9s shows the tractor filling the direction of the approaching car; the overhead render shows the truck crossing between her X and the eastbound lanes. The ray-cast agrees (blocked by veh_T_tractor, 28.3 m to the car). She testified "I had a clear view of the car the whole way in. I watched it right up until the moment it hit. Nothing was in the way." (Depo 27:46).
